title: What is known about 1RB0RC_1LC0LD_1RA0LB_1LE0RA_1RD1LF_0LC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RC_1LC0LD_1RA0LB_1LE0RA_1RD1LF_0LC---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The machine is a particle system on a background of 10s. Lean proves the motion of the moving particle Q exactly (for every size of the tape around it) and that the run from blank tape reaches that picture; the collisions of Q with the other particles are only observed. The C simulator finds no halt in 1010 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 61,189 cells have been visited and 30,446 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Q bounces: exact rules for every size
claims.text: With Q0 a c R = 1 A>1 0 (10)^a 0 (10)^c R and Q1 a c R = 1 A>1 0 (10)^a 1 1 0 (10)^c R (blank tape on the left, any tape R on the right): Q0 a (c+2) R reaches Q1 (a+2) c R in 4a+14 steps and Q1 a (c+1) R reaches Q0 (a+2) (c+1) R in 4a+10 steps, for all a, c and R. The head never looks at R.

claims.title: Q travels one pair per two bounces
claims.text: Q0 a (c+1+2k) R reaches Q0 (a+4k) (c+1) R in exactly 8ak + 16k² + 16k steps: the reflector moves k pairs to the right while the tape grows 4k cells on the left.

claims.title: Blank tape reaches the particle picture
claims.text: After 397 steps from blank tape the configuration is Q0 3 10 R0 (R0 = 0 1 1 0 0 1 1); by travel it is Q0 19 2 R0 at step 813 and, one bounce later (step 903), Q in its long form touches the first stationary particle.

claims.title: No halt in 10<sup>10</sup> steps; the particle picture holds throughout
claims.text: py/snap.c runs 1010 steps without a halt (43 s). At the last left turn (step 9,999,876,324) the tape spans cells −256,550 to 30,857 and reads, in particle form, 3 1^2 0 1513 P 40809 0 12470 P 733 1^2 0 4183 P 7557 P 430 P 1385 P 2985 P ... P 185 P 297 P ... P 59 P 99 ... wall (n = (10)^n): 293 stationary particles P, mostly in lattices with alternating gaps (3, 11) ×52, (9, 41) ×18, (59, 99) ×37, (185, 297) ×27, (555, 899) ×6, (1385, 2985) ×3 (from the right), and a wall (1 0 0 1 1 0 0)^m at the right end.

claims.title: Collisions and the growth in bursts
claims.text: When Q reaches a stationary particle, the two exchange places or merge and a new reflector is sent on; when a Q reaches the wall the right end grows three cells per bounce for a while (bursts at steps 1,366, 96,934, 473,188, 1,276,984 and 1.2×10<sup>9</sup> in the first 3×10<sup>9</sup> steps, the right end at 14, 80, 262, 562, 922 and then growing again). The collision rules are observed in simulation, not proved, so the long-run order of events is open.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.98×10<sup>12</sup> steps of an accelerated run
claims.text: Observed, not proved: the accelerated simulator rsim.py ran 1.98×1012 steps from blank tape without reaching a halting transition. Its tape, state and head position were equal to those of a plain C simulator at 6 checkpoints, the last at 1.02×1010 steps. Of these steps, the part after the last checkpoint rests on the simulator alone, including 493 trip-level jumps: a jump applies many identical round trips at once after seeing the same tape shape recur with constant count changes, which is validated against direct simulation but not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. A proof would need the collision rules of Q with P, with the wall and with the left end, and an invariant on the lattices they build; the only halting transition (F reading 1) cannot occur in the proved bounce rules, which use only states A to D.

claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LC_1RC0RA_1LA0LD_1LE0RB_1RD1LF_0LA--- up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine builds a tape of 10 10 10 ... carrying a few kinds of particles. The head bounces off one of them, a moving reflector, and pushes it to the right; the others stand still and pile up in lattices. Lean proves exactly how the reflector moves; what happens when particles meet is only observed. It has run 1010 steps without stopping.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; the tape spans 287,408 cells.
Exact bounce and travel rules for the reflector, for all sizes.
Background 10, reflector Q, stationary P, wall.
No halt in the accelerated simulator (observed, not proved; checked against direct simulation up to 1.02×10<sup>10</sup> steps).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.546). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 61,189 cells (50,664 left of the start, 922 right), with a density of 1s of 0.498.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: What the tape is made of
html: Almost all of the tape is the pattern 1 0 1 0 1 0 .... A sweep of the head shifts this background by one cell (in state A, A>1 0 becomes 0 1 A>; in states B and C the same happens leftwards), so the head can cross any amount of it at a steady pace. What makes the machine interesting are the places where the pattern is broken, the particles:

• Q, the reflector: a single extra 0 (short form) or an extra 1 1 0 (long form). The head cannot cross it: it bounces back to the left end.
  • P = 0 1 1 0 0, a stationary particle: the head crosses it, and after the round trip it is back in place.
  • the wall (1 0 0 1 1 0 0)^m at the right end, which grows in bursts;
  • the left end 1 1 0 (or (10)^3 1 1 0), which grows by two cells per bounce and from time to time emits a new Q.

sections.heading: One bounce, and how far Q travels
html:
Look at the tape when the head, in state A, stands on the second cell of the tape. With Q in its short or long form the tape is

Q0 a c R = 1 A>1 0 (10)^a 0 (10)^c R
Q1 a c R = 1 A>1 0 (10)^a 1 1 0 (10)^c R

(blank tape on the left, any tape R on the right). One trip of the head to Q and back gives

Q0 a (c+2) R  →  Q1 (a+2) c R        in 4a + 14 steps
Q1 a (c+1) R  →  Q0 (a+2) (c+1) R    in 4a + 10 steps

so every two bounces Q moves one pair to the right and the tape grows four cells on the left. Iterated,

Q0 a (c+1+2k) R  →  Q0 (a+4k) (c+1) R   in 8ak + 16k² + 16k steps.

The head never looks at R, so these hold whatever lies beyond Q; all three are proved in Lean for every a, c, k and R. The trip to Q gets longer as the left part grows, so a reflector that has to cross n pairs takes about 16n² steps: this is where the square-root growth comes from. The same rules hold, with the same proofs, for the sister machine 1RB0RC_1LC0LD_1RA0LB_1LE0RA_1RA1LF_0LC---, which differs only in what E does on a 0.

sections.heading: Particles over a billion steps
html: Each row below is the tape at one left turn of the head (every 40th, up to step 109; time goes down, the left end is the diagonal edge). Grey is visited background, black marks a broken pattern (two equal neighbouring cells). Diagonal lines are reflectors Q moving right; vertical lines are stationary particles P; the black block on the right is the wall.

The run is a sequence of epochs. A reflector is sent off from the left end and travels right; when it meets a P the two interact and the reflector goes on, leaves a particle behind, or is absorbed (then a new one starts at the left end); when one reaches the wall, the right end grows three cells per bounce for a while. The stationary particles end up in regular lattices: at step 1010 the tape reads, in particle form (n stands for (10)^n),

3 1^2 0 1513 P 40809 0 12470 P 733 1^2 0 4183 P 7557 P 430 P 1385 P 2985 P 1385 P ... P 555 P 899 P 555 P ...
  ... P 185 P 297 P 185 P ... P 59 P 99 P 59 P 99 ... (1 0 0 1 1 0 0)^m

with 293 particles P, most of them in lattices whose gaps alternate in pairs: from the right, (3, 11) 52 times, (9, 41) 18 times, (59, 99) 37 times, (185, 297) 27 times, (555, 899) 6 times, (1385, 2985) 3 times. Each lattice is built in one epoch, and each is more widely spaced than the one before. The rules of these collisions are seen in the simulation; they are not proved.

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The only halting transition is F reading 1, and F is entered only from E reading 1. A bounce off the reflector uses only states A to D (E and F never occur in the proved bounce rules), so the machine cannot halt while a reflector travels. A halt would have to come from a collision: a reflector meeting a particle, the wall or the left end in a configuration that has not happened in 1010 steps. Ruling that out needs the full table of collisions and an invariant on the lattices they build.

sections.heading: What is proved
html: Lean, kernel only: bounce0, bounce1, bounce2, travel (with the exact step count tcost_eq) in lean/Macro.lean, from the cell rules bounce0_cells, bounce1_cells (lean/Rules.lean, written by py/gen_rules.py); reach_Q0, reach_travel, reach_P (blank tape reaches Q0 3 10 R0 at step 397) in lean/Reach.lean. Computed: no halt in 1010 steps, the particle form of the tape. Open: the collision rules, and halting.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0LC_1RC0RA_1LA0LD_1LE0RB_1RD1LF_0LA---: rename A→B, B→C, C→A, D→D, E→E, F→F; it is this table started in state C
  • 1RB0LC_1LA1RF_1LD0LE_1RE0RA_1LC0RD_0RE---: rename A→C, B→D, C→E, D→A, E→B, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state D, in a mirror
  • 1RB0RD_1LC0RA_1LA0LB_1RE0LC_1LD1RF_0RB---: rename A→C, B→A, C→B, D→D, E→E, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state B, in a mirror

family: particles in a 10-background (bouncer with a moving reflector)
summary: The tape is a background of 10s carrying particles: a moving reflector Q that the head bounces off and pushes right one pair every two bounces (proved in Lean for all sizes), stationary particles P that pile up in self-similar lattices, and a wall at the right end; open.
